extracted.intended_audience: Users and developers of PARI/GP (mathematicians, computational number theorists, and programmers using the gp calculator or PARI library)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for PARI/GP: syntax conventions, interactive features (completion, help, Emacs integration), and detailed semantics for many standard operators and conversion/utility functions available in PARI/GP (version 2.7.7 in this chunk).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tab-completion behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: If, at any time, only one completion is meaningful, gp will provide it together with an ending comma if completing a default, or a pair of parentheses if completing a function name. Hitting <TAB> again will provide the argument list as given by the online help. Otherwise, hitting <TAB> once more will give you the list of possible completions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: to obtain default(seriesprecision,10) you can type def<TAB>se<TAB>10 (saves keystrokes). Experiment with this mechanism; it is convenient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online help keys
rubrics_metrics.description: M-h gives short online help for the word under the cursor; M-H yields extended help corresponding to the help default program (usually opens a DVI previewer or runs a primitive tex-to-ASCII program).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: None of these disturb the line you were editing. You can undo preceding keys by hitting C-_.

rubrics_metrics.name: PariEmacs autoload setup
rubrics_metrics.description: How to autoload gp-mode, gp-script-mode, gp, and gpman in GNU Emacs via .emacs entries and ensure files with .gp suffix use gp-script-mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add autoload lines and (setq auto-mode-alist (cons '("\\.gp$" . gp-script-mode) auto-mode-alist)). Then use M-x gp to start gp as a subprocess with default stack size and prime limit; use PariEmacs docs for further customizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Function entry notation
rubrics_metrics.description: General entry format: foo(x, {flag = 0}): short description. The library syntax is GEN foo(GEN x, long fl = 0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Braces denote optional arguments. Optional args may be omitted; a comma or closing parenthesis signals use of the default. When more than one optional arg exists, user-supplied values fill arguments in order; empty arguments can be used to skip defaults.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional argument semantics and empty-arg trick
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional arguments are denoted { } and have default values; typing a missing optional argument as a trailing comma or closing parenthesis signals use of the default. To set a later optional argument while keeping earlier defaults, use an empty argument, e.g. foo(6,,1). foo() yields defaults for all optional args.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In special case of no mandatory arguments you may omit parentheses (standalone foo) though not recommended for clarity. Optional args are placed at end in decreasing usefulness so they can usually be ignored.

rubrics_metrics.name: {x}* meaning (varargs)
rubrics_metrics.description: An optional argument between braces followed by a star, like {x }*, means that any number of such arguments (possibly none) can be given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in particular by various print routines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flags: definition and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: A flag is an optional argument that instructs a routine to change default behavior (e.g., return more or less information). Flags do not convey 'data' but toggles/options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two kinds exist: generic and binary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic flags
rubrics_metrics.description: Generic flags: all valid values are individually described (e.g., 'If flag is equal to 1, then...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One may pass the numeric value or its mnemonic string (see mnemonics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Binary flags (bitmask flags)
rubrics_metrics.description: Binary flags use customary binary notation to represent many toggles with a single integer: each bit corresponds to a switch p0,...,pn; numeric sum indicates set toggles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author documents mapping as 'The binary digits of flag mean: 1: p0, 2: p1, 4: p2', etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mnemonics for flags
rubrics_metrics.description: Numeric flags are obscure and rigid; mnemonics (character strings containing symbolic identifiers) may replace numeric flags. For generic flags you can use the mnemonic string instead of the number (e.g., fun(x, 1) or fun(x, "AGM")).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For binary flags, mnemonics for toggles are given and can be negated by prepending no or removing such prefix. Toggles can be grouped with punctuation or bitwise-like notation (e.g., 'Parametric; no Recursive' or 'Parametric | no Recursive'). Mnemonics are recommended when not using gp calculator interactively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pointers (&) in prototypes
rubrics_metrics.description: If a parameter in the function prototype is prefixed with &, as in foo(x, &e), the function may assign a value to e as a side effect. When passing the argument, the & sign must be typed explicitly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As of version 2.7.7 pointer arguments are optional for documented functions and thus appear between brackets like Z_issquare(x, {&e}).

rubrics_metrics.name: Library programming: fixed argument counts
rubrics_metrics.description: When programming with the PARI library, all arguments are mandatory (no variable number of args); variants are usually provided corresponding to various flag values. The prototype includes = default value tokens to signal how a missing argument should be encoded (often NULL pointer or -1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the User’s Guide to the PARI library for background and details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monadic operators + and -
rubrics_metrics.description: The expressions +x and -x refer to monadic operators (the first does nothing, the second negates x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gneg(GEN x) for -x.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dyadic operator + (addition) semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: x + y is the sum. Addition between a scalar and a t_COL or t_MAT returns respectively [y[1] + x, y[2], ...] and y + xId. Other additions between a scalar and a vector/matrix, or between vector/matrices of incompatible sizes are forbidden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gadd(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dyadic operator - (subtraction) semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: x - y is the difference. Subtraction between a scalar and a t_COL or t_MAT returns respectively [y[1] - x, y[2], ...] and y - xId. Other incompatible subtractions are forbidden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gsub(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dyadic operator * (multiplication) semantics and restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: x * y is the product. Multiplication between vector/matrices of incompatible sizes is forbidden; multiplication between two t_VECs or two t_COLs is not allowed. Restricted to scalars some types; * is commutative for scalars but not in general due to vector/matrix ops. Special compositions: binary quadratic forms compose, t_VECSMALL of same length are permutations composed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To take scalar product of two vectors, transpose one and multiply: a * a~. Library syntax: GEN gmul(GEN x, GEN y). GEN gsqr(GEN x) available for x*x.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dyadic operator / (division) semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: x / y is the quotient. If divisor is a matrix it must be an invertible square matrix and result is x * y^{-1}. Result is as exact as possible: integer division yields rational, polynomial division yields rational function. To obtain approximate real quotient add 0., for p-adic add O(p^k), for Taylor series add O(X^k) or use taylor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gdiv(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: Euclidean quotient operator \
rubrics_metrics.description: x \ y is the Euclidean quotient: for real scalar y it's floor(x/y) if y>0 and ceil(x/y) if y<0 when not exact. Remainder x - (x\y)*y is in [0, |y|[. When y integer and x polynomial, y promoted to polynomial deg 0. Applied componentwise on vectors/matrices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gdivent(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rounded Euclidean quotient operator \/
rubrics_metrics.description: x \/ y evaluates to the rounded Euclidean quotient: same as \ except for scalar division where quotient yields remainder smallest in absolute value (ties choose quotient closest to +∞), remainder in ]- |y|/2, |y|/2]. Applied componentwise on vectors/matrices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gdivround(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: Modular remainder operator %
rubrics_metrics.description: x % y evaluates to the modular Euclidean remainder: for non-integral real x or y, defined as x - (x\y)*y. If y integer and x integer, smallest non-negative integer congruent to x modulo y. If y polynomial, polynomial of smallest degree congruent to x modulo y. When y integer and x polynomial, y promoted to polynomial deg 0. Applied componentwise on vectors/matrices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show difference between (1/2) % 3 and 0.5 % 3. Library syntax: GEN gmod(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: Powering operator ^ semantics and special cases
rubrics_metrics.description: x^n is powering. Integer exponent uses exact binary powering; x cannot be vector or matrix unless square (invertible if negative exponent). For non-integer exponents it's treated as transcendental (componentwise powering on vectors/matrices). Rational exponents on t_INTMOD or p-adics attempt to return q-th root if exists (q must not have large prime factors). Negative integer exponents compute inverse; failure on non-invertible t_INTMOD may reveal nontrivial factor of modulus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes about rewriting x * x as x^2 when operands identical in memory; warnings about non-invertible polmods and algorithms that assume base ring is a domain. Library syntax: GEN gpow(GEN x, GEN n, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: cmp(x,y) universal comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: cmp(x,y) returns -1, 0, or 1 for comparison between arbitrary objects. Underlying order is transitive; returns 0 iff x === y. Restriction to integers matches usual order. If components equal up to smallest length, more complex object considered larger: longest is largest; when lengths equal, matrix > vector > scalar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mostly useful to handle sorted lists or vectors of arbitrary objects (e.g., vecsort(v, cmp) equivalent to Set(v)). Library syntax: GEN cmp_universal(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: divrem(x,y,{v})
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates a column vector [Euclidean quotient (x\y), Euclidean remainder (x - (x\y)*y)] of division of x by y. If v present and x,y multivariate polynomials, divide w.r.t variable v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoids doing two divisions if both quotient and remainder needed. Note divrem(x,y)[2] may differ from x % y in general (examples shown). Library syntax: GEN divrem(GEN x, GEN y, long v = -1) and GEN gdiventres(GEN x, GEN y) when v not needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: lex(x,y) lexicographic comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: Gives lexicographic comparison result -1,0,1 between x and y in a wide sense: admissible to compare different types provided scalars can be compared; comparison is recursive. If components equal up to smallest operand length, more complex object is larger (longer largest; when equal lengths matrix > vector > scalar).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided. Library syntax: GEN lexcmp(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: max(x,y) and min(x,y)
rubrics_metrics.description: max(x,y) creates the maximum of x and y when they can be compared; min(x,y) creates the minimum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntaxes: GEN gmax(GEN x, GEN y) and GEN gmin(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: shift(x,n) and shiftmul(x,n)
rubrics_metrics.description: shift(x,n) shifts x componentwise left by n bits if n >= 0 and right by |n| bits if n < 0. Left shift corresponds to multiplication by 2^n; right shift of integer corresponds to Euclidean division by 2^{|n|} with remainder sign same as x. shiftmul(x,n) multiplies x by 2^n; difference: when n<0 shiftmul does ordinary division (may produce fraction), while shift uses Euclidean division and integer stays integer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abbreviations: x << n or x >> (-n). Library syntaxes: GEN gshift(GEN x, long n) and GEN gmul2n(GEN x, long n).

rubrics_metrics.name: sign(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns sign (0, 1 or -1) of x, which must be integer, real or fraction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gsigne(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: vecmax(x, {&v})
rubrics_metrics.description: If x is a vector or matrix returns the largest entry; otherwise returns a copy of x. Error if x empty. If &v provided and x vector, set v to index of largest entry; if x matrix set v to coordinates [i,j].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example queries shown. Library syntax: GEN vecmax0(GEN x, GEN *v = NULL). Also GEN vecmax(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: vecmin(x, {&v})
rubrics_metrics.description: If x is a vector or matrix returns smallest entry; otherwise returns copy of x. Error if x empty. If &v provided, set v to index of smallest entry (or coordinates for matrix).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples shown. Library syntax: GEN vecmin0(GEN x, GEN *v = NULL). Also GEN vecmin(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison and Boolean operators available
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard comparison operators <=, <, >=, >, ==, != available; result 1 if true, 0 if false. == is liberal (0 integer, 0 polynomial, and zero vector considered equal). === tests for identity (much stricter). GP accepts <> as synonym for !=. = is assignment, not equality. Boolean operators ||, &&, ! are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: t_STR objects are strictly larger than other non-string types for comparison; two t_STR compared lexicographically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversions: Col(x,{n})
rubrics_metrics.description: Transforms x into a column vector. If n omitted or 0, dimension depends on type: usually single component, except when x is a vector/quadratic form (becomes row considered as column), polynomial/power series (coefficients used), matrix (column of row vectors comprising matrix), or character string (vector of individual characters). If n given, 0 entries appended/prepended depending on sign; dimension |n|. n meaningless for matrix or char string.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Colrev does not exist; use Vecrev. Library syntax: GEN gtocol0(GEN x, long n) and GEN gtocol(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: Colrev(x,{n})
rubrics_metrics.description: Same as Col(x,n) then reverse the result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gtocolrev0(GEN x, long n). GEN gtocolrev(GEN x) available.

rubrics_metrics.name: List({x = []})
rubrics_metrics.description: Transforms a row/column vector x into a list whose components are entries of x; for other types creates list with single element x (or empty list when x omitted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: except when x omitted, this function creates a small memory leak; initialize lists or use sparingly. Library syntax: GEN gtolist(GEN x = NULL). GEN listcreate(void) creates empty list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mat({x = []})
rubrics_metrics.description: Transforms x into a matrix. If x already matrix, returns copy. If x is row/column vector, creates 1-row/1-column matrix unless elements are column/row vectors of same length, in which case vectors are concatenated into big matrix. Binary quadratic form becomes 2x2 matrix. Otherwise creates 1x1 matrix containing x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples shown. Library syntax: GEN gtomat(GEN x = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mod(a,b) behavior (intmod/polmod/base change)
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates an intmod (a mod b) if b integer or polmod if b polynomial. If a%b makes sense and yields appropriate type operation succeeds. If a is complex object, base change it to Z/bZ or K[x]/(b) — equivalent but faster than multiplying by Mod(1,b). This function is not same as x % y (which has no knowledge of intended modulus).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples compare x = 4 % 5 versus x = Mod(4,5). Library syntax: GEN gmodulo(GEN a, GEN b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pol(t,{v=x})
rubrics_metrics.description: Transforms t into a polynomial with main variable v. If t scalar gives constant polynomial. If t power series with non-negative valuation or rational function behaves like truncate (chop O(X^k) or Euclidean quotient then set main variable). When t is a vector, creates polynomial whose coefficients are given by t with t[1] as leading coefficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pol is faster on vector of coefficients than naive expression. Polrev available if want x[1] as constant term. Warning: not a substitution function; variable priority restrictions apply. Library syntax: GEN gtopoly(GEN t, long v = -1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Polrev(t,{v=x})
rubrics_metrics.description: Transforms t into a polynomial with main variable v. For vectors it creates polynomial with t[1] as constant term (reverse of Pol). For power series acts like truncate. Reciprocal of Pol is Vec (and Polrev <-> Vecrev).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warning same as Pol about variable priority. Library syntax: GEN gtopolyrev(GEN t, long v = -1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Qfb(a,b,c,{D=0.})
rubrics_metrics.description: Creates binary quadratic form ax^2 + bxy + cy^2. If b^2 - 4ac > 0, initialize Shanks' distance function to D. Negative definite forms not implemented; use positive definite counterpart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN Qfb0(GEN a, GEN b, GEN c, GEN D = NULL, long prec). GEN qfi and GEN qfr variants available with sign assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ser(s,{v=x},{d=seriesprecision})
rubrics_metrics.description: Transforms s into a power series with main variable v and precision d (number of significant terms). Scalars become constant series with precision d. If s polynomial truncated to d terms. If s vector, coefficients of vector are understood to be coefficients of series starting from constant term and d ignored (vector length determines terms). If s already power series in v, returned verbatim ignoring d. Not a substitution function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show behavior; to enforce d for vectors/power series convert/truncate to t_POL first. Library syntax: GEN gtoser(GEN s, long v = -1, long precdl).

rubrics_metrics.name: Set({x = []})
rubrics_metrics.description: Converts x into a set (row vector) with strictly increasing entries according to universal cmp. Container types converted to set of elements; others converted to set of one element.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example Set([1,2,4,2,1,3]) yields [1,2,3,4]. Library syntax: GEN gtoset(GEN x = NULL).

rubrics_metrics.name: Str({x}*) and Strchr(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Str concatenates its argument list into a single character string (type t_STR, empty if x omitted); arguments evaluated in string context. Strchr converts integer to character string by translating each integer into a character (e.g., Strchr(97) -> 'a').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To recover GEN from string apply eval. Use strtoGEN/GENtostr in library mode (GENtostr returns malloced string to free). Library syntaxes: GEN gtolist(?)? (Str is mostly useless in library mode); Strchr has library syntax GEN Strchr(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: Strexpand({x}*) for environment expansion
rubrics_metrics.description: Converts args to single string then performs environment expansion (useful to read env variable values).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments read in string context. Example Strexpand('$HOME/doc') -> '/home/pari/doc'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strtex({x}*) to TeX
rubrics_metrics.description: Translates arguments to TeX format and concatenates into a single string.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arguments read in string context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vec(x,{n}) and Vecrev(x,{n}) and Vecsmall(x,{n})
rubrics_metrics.description: Vec transforms x into a row vector; dimension optional. Behavior depends on type (vector/quadratic form, polynomial/power series, matrix, string, error context). Vecrev does Vec then reverse (reciprocal of Polrev). Vecsmall returns a t_VECSMALL row vector where representable as small integers; strings map to ASCII char codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If n given 0 entries appended/prepended. In certain cases n meaningless. Library syntaxes: GEN gtovec0(...), GEN gtovecrev0(...), GEN gtovecsmall0(...), plus simpler variants.

rubrics_metrics.name: binary(x) and bitwise functions
rubrics_metrics.description: binary(x) outputs vector of binary digits of |x|. bitand(x,y) bitwise and of two integers (2-adic behavior for negatives), bitneg(x,{n=-1}) bitwise negation truncated to n bits (n=-1 means no truncation), bitnegimply(x,y) bitwise negated imply (not(x => y)), bitor(x,y) bitwise or, bittest(x,n) outputs nth bit (0/1), bitxor(x,y) bitwise xor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Negative numbers behave 2-adically. Examples provided for bitand and bittest. Library syntaxes provided: GEN binaire, GEN gbitand/ibitand, GEN gbitneg, GEN gbitnegimply/ibitnegimply, GEN gbitor/ibitor, GEN gbittest/ulong int_bit, GEN gbitxor/ibitxor.

rubrics_metrics.name: ceil(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ceiling of x: when x in R, smallest integer >= x. Applied to rational function, returns Euclidean quotient numerator/denominator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gceil(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: centerlift(x,{v})
rubrics_metrics.description: Same as lift except t_INTMOD and t_PADIC components are lifted using centered residues: for t_INTMOD x in Z/nZ lift y with -n/2 < y <= n/2. For t_PADIC lifted similarly if valuation >= 0; if not returns fraction p^v centerlift(x p^{-v}); rational reconstruction not attempted. centerlift(x,'v) alias for lift(x,'v) for backward compatibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: centerlift(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: characteristic(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Returns characteristic of base ring over which x defined (as from t_INTMOD and t_FFELT components). Raises exception if incompatible primes arise from t_FFELT and t_PADIC components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example characteristic(Mod(1,24)*x + Mod(1,18)*y) = 6. Library syntax: GEN characteristic(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: component(x,n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Extracts nth-component of x: components counted after initial code words for each PARI type. For vector it's nth-component, for matrix nth column, for polynomial nth coefficient (degree n-1), for power series nth significant coefficient.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer polcoeff for polynomials and [ ] operator for vectors/matrices. Using component requires detailed knowledge of PARI type structure and should almost never be used. Examples of use for p-adic accuracy shown. Library syntax: GEN compo(GEN x, long n).

rubrics_metrics.name: conj(x) conjugation
rubrics_metrics.description: Conjugate of x. For real quadratic numbers, conjugation in real quadratic field. No effect on integers, reals, intmods, fractions or p-adics. polmod is forbidden (use conjvec for that).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gconj(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: conjvec(z) for polmod conjugates/embeddings
rubrics_metrics.description: Conjugate vector representation of z. If z is a polmod Mod(a,T), returns vector length degree(T) containing either complex embeddings of z if T has rational coefficients (a(r[i]) where r = polroots(T)), or conjugates of z if T has some intmod coefficients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continued description and context in later text (cutoff in this chunk).
